security_privacy_cost_impact: Tightens only. A settled approval request's status, decided_by and decided_at are now frozen for every writer that fires triggers, and an INSERT that names a decider is timed by the database. Probes added or hardened: the verdict ties each refusal to its object and its transaction, psql meta-commands are refused in every SQL source before anything runs, every trigger on approval_requests and the functions they run are pinned, a parameter grant of session_replication_role is refused, and every non-superuser role's privileges on the two calendar tables are held to an allowlist. No grant is added. No secret or customer data.
migration_and_data_impact: ONE MIGRATION: 126_approval_decision_frozen_for_every_writer.sql (replaces private.set_decided_at()'s body, recreates its trigger BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE, adds CHECK (decided_at >= created_at), apply-time block). 125's block superseded by a final-state replacement in db/foundation/invariants/. Declared in the snapshot's not-applied tail. The CHECK applies over no rows: no environment holds approval data before G0.
compatibility_impact: Additive and forward. Cases stay 1058; tests stay 675; the foundation-contract assertion floor 365 -> 418. Probes 12 -> 14. A writer that inserts a decided approval request no longer keeps the decided_at it sent (O3), and no writer that fires triggers can move a request out of a non-pending state (O4).
known_limitations: Blocker 186 (15)'s command-role half: the settled-row closure for an RFC-2026-023 command role waits on that RFC.
Blocker 186 (16), the anonymisation route batch 160 needs, which must now also account for status; (20), INFO, except the transaction-control check now running before the drifts.

A superuser still bypasses the trigger with session_replication_role or DISABLE TRIGGER (caught in a later file by the trigger probe); ALTER SYSTEM is not covered. A hostile superuser drift can still forge in ways no verdict sees.
psqlLex over-refuses a SQL-standard `begin atomic ... end` body (fails closed; no drift uses one).

The grant allowlist covers the two calendar tables only; the general version over every RLS table in app is not attempted. C0 H1's optional case owner-a-cannot-place-an-item-already-deleted is not added.
A5's (h): zone-name case variants and Etc/UTC.
